_Requested by **butch** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01DfXSfaWMc2kCAhrqxCVLKx?thread=cmsg_01DfXSfaWMc2kCAhrqxCVLKx1oPMUpLNschnjLwAKCRdyq)_

Before: Beukers (arXiv:2403.03301v3) proves `F(t) ≡ F_p(t)F(t^σ)` and his CM supercongruences only for families whose weight-two form vanishes to order `r < 1/3`. In Remark 1.14(2) he reports, from computer experiments only, the mod `p²` congruence for Cooper's `s7`, `s10`, `s18` and the Hadamard products Apéry2 ⊙ central and Franel ⊙ central. In Remark 1.17 he says he does not know whether his modular approach works at primes that do not split in the CM field. Chan–Cooper–Sica's Conjecture 5.4 (`c7(pn) ≡ c7(n) mod p²` for the weight-one root of `s7`) is listed as open by Cooper (arXiv:2302.00757v2, §11). HYP-9310 is an open hypothesis.

After:
- `05-knowledge/results/beukers_remark114_power_structure_and_inert_cm_20261018.md` proves Beukers' Remark 1.14(2) for all five families at every `p ∤ N`, his CM Theorems 1.15/1.16 mod `p²` for them, and a new inert-prime theorem: for every family in his setting (Assumption (II) or these five) and every rational CM value `t(α)`, `F_p(t(α)) ≡ 0 (mod p²)` when `p` is inert in `Q(α)`. As a corollary it gives a modular proof of Z.-W. Sun's congruence `Σ_{k<p} A_k ≡ 4x² − 2p` or `0 (mod p²)` for Apéry numbers (first proved by C. Wang and Z.-W. Sun, 2024, with the `p`-adic Gamma function). It also records eight misprints in Beukers' Appendix C.
- `05-knowledge/results/cooper_s7_weight_one_root_frobenius_20261018.md` proves the Chan–Cooper–Sica conjecture in both directions (`c7(pn) ≡ c7(n) mod p²` for all `n` iff `p = 7` or `p ≡ 1, 2, 4 mod 7`), the "only if" half of O'Brien's Lucas conjecture, and a companion congruence at inert primes. It now points to the new note for the other families.
- `05-knowledge/results/hyp9310_is_klmsy_corollary_reflection_proof_20261018.md` shows that HYP-9310's law is Corollary 3 of Kibelbek–Long–Moss–Sheller–Yuan (JNT 2016), with an independent proof. Part (K) stays OPEN.

How (new note): when `t^a Θ^b` is an η-product, the leading coefficient of Beukers' polynomial is an `a`-th power, `T_{p,p+1} = ±Q^a` with `Q ≡ 1 (mod p)` of degree `≤ (p+1)/b`. For these five families `a = b − 1`, and this closes the degree count his Theorem 1.13 cannot close when `r ≥ 1/3`. At inert primes, Shimura's reciprocity law makes the inertia group at `p` act on the `p+1` roots of `T_p(x, t(α))` through a non-split Cartan subgroup, which is transitive on `P¹(F_p)`; so all roots have valuation `2p/(p+1)`, which forces `F_p(t(α)) ≡ 0 (mod p²)`.

Checks: `gp -q 04-computation/experiments/beukers_remark114_power_structure_check_20261018.gp` (16 s) verifies the identities, Lemma 1 for `p ≤ 61`, Theorem 1 for `p < 110`, 24 Newton polygons, all 118 rational CM values of Beukers' Appendix C for `5 ≤ p < 400` (4600 inert, 4268 split, 38 ramified prime-value pairs) and Sun's congruence for `p < 400`. `gp -q 04-computation/experiments/cooper_s7_weight1_frobenius_check_20261018.gp` (3.5 min) checks the `s7` note. Both outputs are committed and every check prints 1.

Typing: PROVED (Lemma 1, Theorems 1, 3, 4, Corollaries 2, 5 of the new note; Theorems A, B, C(ii), D, E, Corollary F of the `s7` note), CITED (Beukers' `T_p` construction and Proposition 5.1, Shimura's reciprocity law, Beukers–Tsai–Ye, Cooper 2012, Babbage), FINITE-EXACT (the checks), VERIFIED only numerically (the congruence at `p | N`; valuation 1 at ramified primes), OPEN (higher powers `p^{2r}`, primes `p | N`, ramified primes, level 11). Every congruence fails mod `p³`. No canonical THM/HYP files or IDs are created or changed.

…roved: c7(pn) == c7(n) mod p^2 iff p = 7 or (p/7) = 1; Beukers' mod p^2 congruence for s7

Work with G = sqrt(F) = theta(x^2+xy+2y^2) on Gamma0(7), whose Hauptmodul t
lives on Gamma0(7)+. Beukers' weight-one T_p polynomial has W7-eigen
coefficients in Z[t] + s Z[t] (s^2 = (1+t)(1-27t)) of degree <= m/3, which
closes the degree count Beukers' Theorem 1.13 cannot close for s7.

- Theorem B: G == G_p G(t^sigma) mod p^2 (split p); G/s == H_p G(t^sigma)
  (inert p). Theorem A: F == F_p F(t^sigma) mod p^2 for every p != 7
  (Beukers, Remark 1.14(2): previously experimental).
- Theorem C: c7 has the Lucas property mod p iff p = 7 or (p/7) = 1; the
  "only if" half (O'Brien 9.2) is new, the "if" half is BTY 2025.
- Theorem D (Chan-Cooper-Sica 2010, Conj. 5.4; O'Brien 9.3): Cartier
  reduction C(G) == G + p C(eps_p G_p) theta G, Lemma E
  (prod(1-q^pn)/prod(1-q^n)^p == E_{p-1}^{-1/2} mod p^2), Proposition F and
  Lemma W (Atkin-Lehner on (E_{p-1}(tau)+E_{p-1}(7tau))/2theta^{p-1});
  p = 2 and p = 7 by Sturm-bounded identities and U_7 on a weight-3
  Eisenstein series; inert primes fail mod p.
- Theorem E: at inert p, d7(pn) == c7(n) mod p^2 for G/s = sum d7(n) t^n.
- Corollary F: Beukers' Theorems 1.15/1.16 hold for s7 mod p^2.
All ingredients checked (split 11..43, inert 5..41, p = 2, 3, 7); every
statement for p < 60 (CM table p < 400); all fail mod p^3.

…both Hadamard products (T_{p,p+1} is an a-th power); inert CM primes F_p(t(alpha)) == 0 mod p^2 for all of Beukers' third-order families

- Lemma 1: when t^a Theta^b is an eta-product, T_{p,p+1} = (-1)^(p+1) Q^a with
  Q in 1 + pZ[t], deg Q <= floor((p+1)/b). With a = b - 1 this closes the
  degree count that Beukers' Theorem 1.13 cannot close for r >= 1/3, giving
  F(t) == F_p(t) F(t^sigma) mod p^2 for s7, s10, s18, Apery2*central and
  Franel*central at every p not dividing N (a second proof for s7).
- Split CM primes: Beukers' Theorems 1.15/1.16 hold mod p^2 for these five.
- Theorem 4 (inert CM primes, Beukers' Remark 1.17): via Shimura reciprocity
  the inertia group at p permutes all p+1 roots of T_p(x, t(alpha)) transitively,
  so they share the valuation 2p/(p+1) and F_p(t(alpha)) == 0 mod p^2.
- Corollary: a new (modular) proof of Z.-W. Sun's congruence for
  sum_{k<p} A_k mod p^2 (first proved by C. Wang and Z.-W. Sun, 2024).
- Eight misprints in Beukers' Appendix C (arXiv v3) corrected and recorded.
- FINITE-EXACT: identities n <= 120; Lemma 1 for p <= 61; Theorem 1 for
  p < 110; 24 Newton polygons; all 118 rational CM values of Appendix C for
  5 <= p < 400 (4600 inert, 4268 split, 38 ramified prime-value pairs).
- The s7 note now points to the new note for these cases.
